deities: Goddess Tarna Devi / Shyama Kali (incarnation of Goddess Parvati)
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (the Mandi Shivaratri Fair's deities converge at this hilltop)

history.summary: Tarna Devi Temple, also called Shyama Kali Temple, stands atop Tarna Hill overlooking Mandi town, reached by 305 stairs from the main bazaar (also motorable). Multiple sources date it to the 17th century and credit Raja Shyam Sen (r. 1664-1675), a devotee of Kali, who is said to have built it after defeating the king of Suket with the goddess's blessing. One source (templeyatri.in) instead credits Raja Ajber Sen as a 17th-century builder — a genuine conflict, since Ajber Sen is otherwise placed in the 16th century. The garbhagriha was significantly renovated in the 19th century by Raja Balbir Singh with gold-and-glass work by artists from Jaipur; legend says the Devi appeared to him as a young girl while he was imprisoned in Amritsar. The black-stone murti is three-faced and wears a silver crown; walls carry paintings of Shiva, Kali and the gurus. Coordinates are POI-matched from map.geocode.

name: Tarna Devi Temple
town_description: Mandi is a historic town on the Beas River and the headquarters of Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. Known as 'Chhoti Kashi' (Varanasi of the Hills), it hosts some 81 old temples and is the venue of the famous Mandi Shivaratri Fair.

travel.railway: Joginder Nagar (narrow gauge) and Shimla (narrow gauge); broad-gauge connections at Chandigarh/Kalka
travel.road: Road from Mandi main bazaar up Tarna Hill, or climb the 305-stair path

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri for peak devotional activity
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not verified in sources; temple accessible during daytime hours
